rationale:
Split: yes, into two independent children along the single seam of the supplied 10-step proof. The selected node then keeps only a 21-line assembly. That assembly also carries out the test-field part of Step 7, using its own declared dependency weighted_mono_radial_test_field.

Why split. The supplied proof bundles two obligations of different kinds that share nothing but an interface:
(A) Steps 1–6, the local data. This part is varifold-specific: a compactness/thickening argument for the room R > ρ, continuity of h and ∇h on B_R(ξ), measurability of ∇^M h and q_ξ from the hypothesis on p_x, and L¹ of H on the compact K = tsupport h ∩ B_R(ξ) ⊆ U. It involves no first variation, no cutoff and no τ.
(B) Steps 7–10, after (RFV) has been applied to γ = φ(·/τ). This part is pure measure-theoretic regrouping. It is stated V-free, for an arbitrary measure μ finite on compacts and functions h, q, g, H, as five of the parent's six children are. It uses no C¹ of h, no openness of U, no integrability of H and no q ≥ 0.
Neither child uses the other. I do not claim reuse elsewhere in the DAG; the split is justified by size and by this clean seam. The whole node compiled to about 260 Lean lines (122 + 116 + 21 non-blank). That is roughly twice the largest atomic sibling (cutoff_integral_deriv, about 140 lines), while each child is in the usual atomic range. The pattern matches this run's accepted 2-way split of regular_set_cover.

subproblems.title: Local data on a larger ball: room, bounds, measurability and integrability (parent Steps 1–6)
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ and E := Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Euclidean, with its Borel σ-algebra). Let V be a rectifiable n-varifold in E with weight μ := V.weight such that μ is finite on compact sets (IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ) and the map x ↦ p_x := (T_xV).starProjection (a continuous linear map E → E) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. Let U ⊆ E be open, H : E → E locally μ-integrable on U (LocallyIntegrableOn H U μ), h : E → ℝ with h ∈ C¹(U) (ContDiffOn ℝ 1 h U), ξ ∈ E and ρ > 0 with tsupport h ∩ B_ρ(ξ) ⊆ U, where B_s(ξ) := closedBall ξ s is the closed ball. Write q := V.normalRadialSq ξ, i.e. q(x) = |p_{(T_xV)^⊥}(x − ξ)|²/|x − ξ|² (Lean convention a/0 = 0), and ∇^M h := V.tangentialGradient h, i.e. ∇^M h(x) = p_x(∇h(x)) with ∇h := gradient h. Then there exist real numbers R and A such that: (a) ρ < R; (b) tsupport h ∩ B_R(ξ) ⊆ U; (c) h and q are a.e. strongly measurable with respect to μ restricted to B_R(ξ); (d) |h(x)| ≤ A and |q(x)| ≤ 1 for every x ∈ B_R(ξ); (e) x ↦ ⟨x − ξ, ∇^M h(x)⟩ is μ-integrable on B_R(ξ); (f) G(x) := ⟨x − ξ, ∇^M h(x) + h(x)H(x)⟩ is μ-integrable on B_R(ξ).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ) (U : Set (Ambient n ℓ)) (H : Ambient n ℓ → Ambient n ℓ) (h : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ) (ξ : Ambient n ℓ) (ρ : ℝ), IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts V.weight → AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x ↦ (V.tangentSpace x).starProjection) V.weight → IsOpen U → LocallyIntegrableOn H U V.weight → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 h U → tsupport h ∩ closedBall ξ ρ ⊆ U → 0 < ρ → ∃ R A : ℝ, ρ < R ∧ tsupport h ∩ closedBall ξ R ⊆ U ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable h (V.weight.restrict (closedBall ξ R)) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable (V.normalRadialSq ξ) (V.weight.restrict (closedBall ξ R)) ∧ (∀ x ∈ closedBall ξ R, |h x| ≤ A ∧ |V.normalRadialSq ξ x| ≤ 1) ∧ IntegrableOn (fun x ↦ inner ℝ (x - ξ) (V.tangentialGradient h x)) (closedBall ξ R) V.weight ∧ IntegrableOn (fun x ↦ inner ℝ (x - ξ) (V.tangentialGradient h x + h x • H x)) (closedBall ξ R) V.weight
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. E := Ambient n ℓ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin (n+ℓ)) is a proper, second-countable Euclidean space with its Borel σ-algebra; μ := V.weight; B_s := closedBall ξ s (closed ball); p_x := (T_xV).starProjection, the orthogonal projection onto T_xV, a continuous linear map E → E; Dh(x) := fderiv ℝ h x; ∇h := gradient h, so ∇h(x) = (toDual ℝ E)⁻¹(Dh(x)), where toDual ℝ E is the Riesz linear isometric equivalence E ≃ E*; ∇^M h(x) = p_x(∇h(x)); q(x) = |p_{(T_xV)^⊥}(x − ξ)|²/|x − ξ|². Of H only its local μ-integrability on U is used.
1. (Room.) The set W := (E ∖ tsupport h) ∪ U is open, since tsupport h is closed and U is open. We have B_ρ ⊆ W: if x ∈ B_ρ lies in tsupport h then x ∈ tsupport h ∩ B_ρ ⊆ U, and otherwise x ∈ E ∖ tsupport h. B_ρ is compact because E is proper. So by IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open there is δ > 0 with cthickening δ B_ρ ⊆ W. Since δ ≥ 0 and ρ ≥ 0, cthickening δ B_ρ = B_{δ+ρ} (cthickening_closedBall). Put R := δ + ρ. Then ρ < R, which is (a); also R ≥ 0 and B_R ⊆ W. If x ∈ tsupport h ∩ B_R, then x ∈ W but x ∉ E ∖ tsupport h, so x ∈ U. This is (b). Consequently every x ∈ B_R with x ∉ U satisfies x ∉ tsupport h.
2. (Continuity of h and ∇h on B_R.) Let x ∈ B_R.
- Case x ∈ U. U is a neighbourhood of x, so h is continuous at x (ContDiffOn.continuousOn, ContinuousOn.continuousAt). Dh is continuous on U by ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen (U open, order 1 ≥ 1), hence continuous at x. Since (toDual ℝ E)⁻¹ is continuous, ∇h = (toDual ℝ E)⁻¹ ∘ Dh is continuous at x.
- Case x ∉ U. By step 1, x ∉ tsupport h, so the open set E ∖ tsupport h is a neighbourhood of x. At every y in it, h(y) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and Dh(y) = 0 (fderiv_of_notMem_tsupport), hence ∇h(y) = (toDual ℝ E)⁻¹(0) = 0. So h and ∇h coincide near x with the constant 0, and both are continuous at x.
Continuity at every point of B_R gives continuity of h and ∇h on B_R.
3. (Bounds and measurability of h and ∇h.) B_R is compact, so by IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn there are A, A₁ ∈ ℝ with |h(x)| ≤ A and |∇h(x)| ≤ A₁ for all x ∈ B_R. B_R is closed, hence measurable, and h, ∇h are continuous on B_R. So both are a.e. strongly measurable for μ⌞B_R (ContinuousOn.aestronglyMeasurable). This gives the h-parts of (c) and (d). Moreover μ(B_R) < ∞, because B_R is compact and μ is finite on compact sets.
4. (∇^M h.) The evaluation map (L, v) ↦ L v on (E →L[ℝ] E) × E is continuous (isBoundedBilinearMap_apply). The map x ↦ p_x is μ-a.e. strongly measurable by hypothesis, hence μ⌞B_R-a.e. strongly measurable, and ∇h is μ⌞B_R-a.e. strongly measurable by step 3. By Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂, ∇^M h(x) = p_x(∇h(x)) is μ⌞B_R-a.e. strongly measurable. An orthogonal projection does not increase norms (Submodule.norm_starProjection_apply_le), so |∇^M h(x)| ≤ |∇h(x)| ≤ A₁ for x ∈ B_R.
5. (q.) For every x the orthogonal projection onto (T_xV)^⊥ is 1 − p_x (Submodule.starProjection_orthogonal'), so q(x) = |(1 − p_x)(x − ξ)|²/|x − ξ|².
- x ↦ 1 − p_x is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (a constant minus an a.e. strongly measurable map), and x ↦ x − ξ is continuous. By continuity of evaluation, as in step 4, x ↦ (1 − p_x)(x − ξ) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, and so are its norm and the square of its norm.
- The denominator x ↦ |x − ξ|² is continuous, hence measurable.
- A quotient of two a.e.-measurable real functions is a.e.-measurable (AEMeasurable.div), and a.e.-measurable real-valued functions are a.e. strongly measurable. So q is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, hence μ⌞B_R-a.e. strongly measurable. This is the q-part of (c).
For every x, q(x) ≥ 0, being a quotient of squares. Also |p_{(T_xV)^⊥}(x − ξ)| ≤ |x − ξ| (Submodule.norm_starProjection_apply_le), so the numerator is at most the denominator. Since a/b ≤ 1 whenever a ≤ b and 0 ≤ b, including b = 0 where a/b = 0 (div_le_one_of_le₀), we get 0 ≤ q(x) ≤ 1, so |q(x)| ≤ 1. This is the q-part of (d).
6. (The ∇^M h term, (e).) F₁(x) := ⟨x − ξ, ∇^M h(x)⟩ is μ⌞B_R-a.e. strongly measurable: the inner product is continuous, x ↦ x − ξ is continuous, and ∇^M h is μ⌞B_R-a.e. strongly measurable by step 4 (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂). For x ∈ B_R, Cauchy–Schwarz gives |F₁(x)| ≤ |x − ξ|·|∇^M h(x)| ≤ R·A₁, using |x − ξ| ≤ R, |∇^M h(x)| ≤ A₁ and R ≥ 0. Since μ(B_R) < ∞, F₁ is μ-integrable on B_R (IntegrableOn.of_bound). This is (e).
7. (The H term.) K := tsupport h ∩ B_R is compact, being a closed subset of the compact B_R, and K ⊆ U by (b). As H is locally μ-integrable on U, H is μ-integrable on K (LocallyIntegrableOn.integrableOn_compact_subset). Let F₂(x) := h(x)⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩.
- F₂ is μ⌞K-a.e. strongly measurable. h is μ⌞B_R-a.e. strongly measurable and μ⌞K ≤ μ⌞B_R. H is μ⌞K-a.e. strongly measurable because it is μ-integrable on K, so ⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩ is too, by continuity of the inner product. Products preserve a.e. strong measurability.
- For x ∈ K we have |h(x)| ≤ A (so A ≥ 0) and |⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩| ≤ |x − ξ||H(x)| ≤ R|H(x)|. Hence |F₂(x)| ≤ (A·R)|H(x)|, and x ↦ (A·R)|H(x)| is μ-integrable on K. By domination (Integrable.mono'), F₂ is μ-integrable on K.
- If x ∈ B_R ∖ K then x ∉ tsupport h, so h(x) = 0 and F₂(x) = 0. As B_R is measurable, F₂ is μ-integrable on B_R (IntegrableOn.of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero).
8. (G, (f), conclusion.) For every x, additivity of the inner product in its second argument and ⟨u, a v⟩ = a⟨u, v⟩ for real a (inner_add_right, inner_smul_right) give G(x) = ⟨x − ξ, ∇^M h(x)⟩ + ⟨x − ξ, h(x)H(x)⟩ = F₁(x) + F₂(x). By steps 6 and 7, F₁ + F₂ is μ-integrable on B_R. Integrability on the measurable set B_R transfers along this pointwise equality (IntegrableOn.congr_fun), which is (f). Steps 1, 3, 5, 6 and 8 give (a)–(f) with these R and A.
proof_key_steps: Room: B_ρ(ξ) lies in the open set W := (E ∖ tsupport h) ∪ U. By compactness some cthickening δ B_ρ(ξ) = B_{ρ+δ}(ξ) ⊆ W. Then R := ρ + δ gives ρ < R and tsupport h ∩ B_R(ξ) ⊆ U, and points of B_R(ξ) ∖ U lie off tsupport h

h and ∇h = (toDual)⁻¹ ∘ Dh are continuous at each point of B_R(ξ): C¹ on the open U, identically 0 near points off tsupport h. Hence they are bounded by A, A₁ on the compact ball and μ⌞B_R-a.e. strongly measurable; μ(B_R(ξ)) < ∞
∇^M h = p_x(∇h) is μ⌞B_R-a.e. strongly measurable (continuous evaluation) with |∇^M h| ≤ A₁ on B_R(ξ)
q = |(1 − p_x)(x − ξ)|²/|x − ξ|² is μ-a.e. strongly measurable and satisfies 0 ≤ q ≤ 1
⟨x − ξ, ∇^M h⟩ is measurable and bounded by R·A₁ on B_R(ξ), so it is μ-integrable there

H is μ-integrable on the compact K = tsupport h ∩ B_R(ξ) ⊆ U. h⟨x − ξ, H⟩ is dominated by A·R·|H| on K and vanishes on B_R(ξ) ∖ K, so it is μ-integrable on B_R(ξ). Hence G = ⟨x − ξ, ∇^M h⟩ + h⟨x − ξ, H⟩ is μ-integrable on B_R(ξ)

subproblems.title: Cutoff identity from the radial first-variation identity along γ = φ(·/τ), for a general measure (parent Steps 7–10)
subproblems.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E := Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ} with its Borel σ-algebra, μ a measure on E that is finite on compact sets, U ⊆ E any set, h, q : E → ℝ, g, H : E → E, φ : ℝ → ℝ of class C¹, ξ ∈ E and c, τ, R, A ∈ ℝ. Write r = r(x) := |x − ξ|, B := B_R(ξ) = closedBall ξ R (closed ball), φ' := deriv φ, γ(t) := φ(t/τ), γ' := deriv γ and G(x) := ⟨x − ξ, g(x) + h(x)H(x)⟩. Assume: (i) tsupport h ∩ B ⊆ U; (ii) g(x) = 0 for every x ∉ tsupport h; (iii) h and q are a.e. strongly measurable with respect to μ restricted to B; (iv) |h(x)| ≤ A and |q(x)| ≤ 1 for every x ∈ B; (v) x ↦ ⟨x − ξ, g(x)⟩ and G are μ-integrable on B; (vi) φ(t) = 0 for every t ≥ c; (vii) τ > 0 and cτ ≤ R; (viii) (RFV_τ) ∫_U [h(x)(n·φ(r/τ) + r·γ'(r)·(1 − q(x))) + φ(r/τ)⟨x − ξ, g(x)⟩] dμ(x) = −∫_U h(x)φ(r/τ)⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩ dμ(x), where ∫_U is the Bochner integral with respect to μ restricted to U. Then n·∫_E h(x)φ(r/τ) dμ + ∫_E h(x)(1 − q(x))·((r/τ)φ'(r/τ)) dμ + ∫_E φ(r/τ)G(x) dμ = 0 (Bochner integrals over E).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)) (U : Set (Ambient n ℓ)) (h q : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ) (g H : Ambient n ℓ → Ambient n ℓ) (φ : ℝ → ℝ) (ξ : Ambient n ℓ) (c τ R A : ℝ), IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ → tsupport h ∩ closedBall ξ R ⊆ U → (∀ x, x ∉ tsupport h → g x = 0) → AEStronglyMeasurable h (μ.restrict (closedBall ξ R)) → AEStronglyMeasurable q (μ.restrict (closedBall ξ R)) → (∀ x ∈ closedBall ξ R, |h x| ≤ A ∧ |q x| ≤ 1) → IntegrableOn (fun x ↦ inner ℝ (x - ξ) (g x)) (closedBall ξ R) μ → IntegrableOn (fun x ↦ inner ℝ (x - ξ) (g x + h x • H x)) (closedBall ξ R) μ → ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → (∀ t, c ≤ t → φ t = 0) → 0 < τ → c * τ ≤ R → ∫ x in U, (h x * ((n : ℝ) * φ (‖x - ξ‖ / τ) + ‖x - ξ‖ * deriv (fun t ↦ φ (t / τ)) ‖x - ξ‖ * (1 - q x)) + φ (‖x - ξ‖ / τ) * inner ℝ (x - ξ) (g x)) ∂μ = -∫ x in U, h x * φ (‖x - ξ‖ / τ) * inner ℝ (x - ξ) (H x) ∂μ → (n : ℝ) * ∫ x, h x * φ (‖x - ξ‖ / τ) ∂μ + ∫ x, h x * (1 - q x) * (‖x - ξ‖ / τ * deriv φ (‖x - ξ‖ / τ)) ∂μ + ∫ x, φ (‖x - ξ‖ / τ) * inner ℝ (x - ξ) (g x + h x • H x) ∂μ = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Conventions. Notation is as in the statement. All integrals are Bochner integrals with respect to μ, with ∫_U taken with respect to μ restricted to U, and "integrable" means μ-integrable on E unless a set is named. Hypothesis (viii) is the first-variation identity tested with the radial field (h(x)φ(|x − ξ|/τ))(x − ξ); the proof only rewrites it.
1. (φ and φ'.) Since φ ∈ C¹, φ is differentiable (ContDiff.differentiable) and φ' is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_deriv). If t > c, then (c, ∞) is an open neighbourhood of t on which φ ≡ 0 by (vi), so φ'(t) = 0 (Filter.EventuallyEq.deriv_eq, deriv_const).
2. (Outside B.) If x ∉ B then r > R ≥ cτ by (vii), so r/τ > c since τ > 0. By (vi) and step 1, φ(r/τ) = 0 and φ'(r/τ) = 0.
3. (Chain rule.) Let s ∈ ℝ. The map t ↦ t/τ has derivative 1/τ at s, and φ is differentiable at s/τ. So t ↦ φ(t/τ) has derivative φ'(s/τ)·(1/τ) at s (HasDerivAt.comp), i.e. γ'(s) = φ'(s/τ)/τ. In particular r·γ'(r) = (r/τ)φ'(r/τ).
4. (Off tsupport h.) If x ∉ tsupport h then h(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and g(x) = 0 by (ii).
5. (From U to E.) Let L(x) := h(x)(n·φ(r/τ) + r·γ'(r)·(1 − q(x))) + φ(r/τ)⟨x − ξ, g(x)⟩ and Q(x) := h(x)φ(r/τ)⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩ be the two integrands of (viii). Let x ∉ U; by (i), x ∉ tsupport h or x ∉ B.
- If x ∉ tsupport h, then by step 4, L(x) = 0·(…) + φ(r/τ)⟨x − ξ, 0⟩ = 0 and Q(x) = 0.
- If x ∉ B, then by steps 2 and 3, φ(r/τ) = 0 and γ'(r) = φ'(r/τ)/τ = 0. So L(x) = h(x)(n·0 + r·0·(1 − q(x))) + 0 = 0 and Q(x) = h(x)·0·⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩ = 0.
So both integrands vanish outside U, hence ∫_U L dμ = ∫_E L dμ and ∫_U Q dμ = ∫_E Q dμ (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero; no measurability of U is needed). Now (viii) reads ∫L dμ = −∫Q dμ.
6. (Bounds on B.) μ(B) < ∞, since B is compact and μ is finite on compact sets. φ and φ' are continuous and [0, R/τ] is compact, so there are M₀, M₁ with |φ(t)| ≤ M₀ and |φ'(t)| ≤ M₁ for t ∈ [0, R/τ] (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn). For x ∈ B we have 0 ≤ r ≤ R, hence r/τ ∈ [0, R/τ], R ≥ 0, |φ(r/τ)| ≤ M₀, |φ'(r/τ)| ≤ M₁ and |r/τ| ≤ R/τ. The functions x ↦ r/τ, x ↦ φ(r/τ) and x ↦ φ'(r/τ) are continuous, hence μ⌞B-a.e. strongly measurable.
7. (Integrability of the pieces.) Put T₁(x) := h(x)φ(r/τ), T₂(x) := h(x)(1 − q(x))·((r/τ)φ'(r/τ)), T₃(x) := φ(r/τ)⟨x − ξ, g(x)⟩ and T₄(x) := φ(r/τ)G(x). By step 2 each Tᵢ vanishes outside B.
- T₁ is μ⌞B-a.e. strongly measurable, as the product of h (by (iii)) and x ↦ φ(r/τ) (step 6). On B, |T₁| ≤ A·M₀ by (iv) and step 6 (A ≥ |h(x)| ≥ 0).
- T₂ is μ⌞B-a.e. strongly measurable, as the product of h and 1 − q (by (iii)) with x ↦ (r/τ)φ'(r/τ) (step 6). Since |1 − q(x)| ≤ 1 + |q(x)| ≤ 2 by (iv), |T₂| ≤ A·2·((R/τ)·M₁) on B.
- As μ(B) < ∞, T₁ and T₂ are μ-integrable on B (IntegrableOn.of_bound).
- T₃ and T₄ are the functions ⟨x − ξ, g⟩ and G, μ-integrable on B by (v), multiplied by φ(r/τ), which is μ⌞B-a.e. strongly measurable and bounded by M₀ μ⌞B-a.e. Hence T₃ and T₄ are μ-integrable on B (Integrable.bdd_mul).
A function that is μ-integrable on B and vanishes outside B is μ-integrable on E (IntegrableOn.integrable_of_forall_notMem_eq_zero). So T₁, T₂, T₃ and T₄ are integrable.
8. (Assembly.) By step 3, L(x) = n·T₁(x) + T₂(x) + T₃(x) pointwise: h(nφ(r/τ) + r(φ'(r/τ)/τ)(1 − q)) + φ(r/τ)⟨x − ξ, g⟩ = n·hφ(r/τ) + h(1 − q)((r/τ)φ'(r/τ)) + φ(r/τ)⟨x − ξ, g⟩ (ring). By linearity of the integral for integrable functions (integral_add, integral_const_mul), ∫L = n∫T₁ + ∫T₂ + ∫T₃. Also Q(x) = T₄(x) − T₃(x) pointwise, because ⟨x − ξ, g + hH⟩ = ⟨x − ξ, g⟩ + h⟨x − ξ, H⟩ (inner_add_right, inner_smul_right); hence ∫Q = ∫T₄ − ∫T₃ (integral_sub). Substituting into ∫L = −∫Q from step 5 gives n∫T₁ + ∫T₂ + ∫T₃ = −∫T₄ + ∫T₃, i.e. n∫T₁ + ∫T₂ + ∫T₄ = 0. This is the claimed identity n∫hφ(r/τ)dμ + ∫h(1 − q)((r/τ)φ'(r/τ))dμ + ∫φ(r/τ)G dμ = 0.
proof_key_steps: φ' is continuous and vanishes on (c, ∞); for x ∉ B_R(ξ), r/τ > c, so φ(r/τ) = φ'(r/τ) = 0
Chain rule: deriv(t ↦ φ(t/τ))(s) = φ'(s/τ)/τ, so r·γ'(r) = (r/τ)φ'(r/τ). Off tsupport h, h = 0 and g = 0
Both (RFV_τ) integrands vanish off U (off tsupport h, or off B_R(ξ)), so ∫_U = ∫_E

T₁ = hφ(r/τ) and T₂ = h(1 − q)(r/τ)φ'(r/τ) are measurable and bounded on B_R(ξ) (|1 − q| ≤ 2). T₃ = φ(r/τ)⟨x − ξ, g⟩ and T₄ = φ(r/τ)G are integrable on B_R(ξ) via a bounded multiplier. All four vanish outside B_R(ξ), so all are μ-integrable
Pointwise L = nT₁ + T₂ + T₃ and Q = T₄ − T₃; linearity turns ∫L = −∫Q into n∫T₁ + ∫T₂ + ∫T₄ = 0
